changes: Add the triangle area formula, one half times base times height, so students can find the cross-section of a triangular prism rather than being given its area.
match.reason: The bank point teaches the same idea of volume as cross-section area times length for rectangular and triangular prisms at the Year 7 depth, but it does not state the triangle area formula that the new point relies on.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point covers both rectangular and triangular prisms and gives the triangle's area ready-made, while this point is only about triangular prisms and needs students to work out ½ × b × h first, so it is narrower and adds a step.

draft.title: Volume of triangular prisms
card: A right prism has the same cross-section all the way along its length. For a triangular prism, the cross-section is a triangle.
Volume of a right prism \(=\) area of cross-section \(\times\) length. The length is the distance between the two triangle ends.

For a triangular prism, the cross-section area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h\). So the volume is \(\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h \times \text{length}\). Here \(h\) is the height of the triangle, at right angles to its base.
A triangle has base 6 cm and height 4 cm, and the prism is 10 cm long. Triangle area: \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12\) cm\(^{2}\). Volume: \(12 \times 10 = 120\) cm\(^{3}\).
draft.remember: Find the area of the triangle end first, then multiply by the length of the prism.

a.q: A triangular prism has a triangle end with base 8 cm and height 5 cm. The prism is 6 cm long. What is its volume?
a.why: The triangle area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20\) cm\(^{2}\). Then \(20 \times 6 = 120\) cm\(^{3}\). The option of \(240\) cm\(^{3}\) is what you get if you forget the half.
a.clue: Find the area of the triangle end first.

b.q: Priya builds a wooden wedge shaped like a triangular prism. Its triangle end has base 10 cm and height 3 cm. The wedge is 12 cm long. What is its volume?
b.why: The triangle area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 3 = 15\) cm\(^{2}\). The volume is \(15 \times 12 = 180\) cm\(^{3}\). The option of \(360\) cm\(^{3}\) comes from leaving out the half, and \(15\) cm\(^{3}\) stops after the triangle area.
b.clue: The length of the prism is not part of the triangle.

wants.brief: A right triangular prism lying on one of its rectangular faces. One triangle end is shaded and labelled cross-section. The base b and the perpendicular height h of the triangle are marked with a right angle symbol. The distance between the two triangle ends is marked length.
wants.why: It shows which triangle is the cross-section and which measure is the length.

problems.detail: The right answer, 120 cm³, is the same as the worked example's answer on the card, so a student could pick it from memory of the example without doing the working. Changing the numbers so the answer differs from 120 would avoid this.

check.summary: Both answers check out: (a) is 120 cm³ and (b) is 180 cm³. The only issue is minor: question (a)'s answer matches the card's worked example (120 cm³), which could let a student guess it without working.
